claims: Positive oracle rewards require strict verified surplus after same-update PnL, spam value, overlap, and safety margin are subtracted.
If recapturable terms dominate verified oracle benefit, any non-negative oracle reward bounded by net benefit is zero.
Risky oracle operations imply settlement admissibility, and settlement admissibility implies quote admissibility.
Positive rewardable oracle-class transitions require strict improvement in the bounded oracle risk lattice.
Rewardable transitions into the risky-ops class cannot pay again when the source state already enabled risky ops.
The production floor-division oracle sync predicate implies the formal cross-multiplication predicate with a one-basis-point budget expansion.
Cross-module extraction is bounded by collateral times divergence budget over the BPS scale.
Fee and parameter-selection theorems give sufficient conditions for fees or configured budgets to dominate bounded oracle divergence extraction.
proof_method: integer arithmetic over net-benefit and overlap-reserved reward budgets

boundaries: OracleSyncGateSoundness models the documented floor-division production predicate and proves bounds with a D+1 basis-point expansion; it does not prove every runtime caller uses the gate.
The oracle benefit proofs assume faithful accounting of risk reduction, same-update PnL, spam value, overlap, and safety margin.
The risk-class lattice is a finite local rewardability model, not a complete oracle governance or market-equilibrium proof.
